quotes.text: offer all five to the honorable, return half to the giver, but surrender not a single ember to the faithless dark.
Yet when a grasping shadow stood at the lower altar, waiting to hoard the light, the Weaver held his five embers close against his breast.
Though shadows whispered temptations of solitary wealth, the Keeper knew that keeping all would extinguish future dawns
to the Hermit who hoarded or the thief who seized without return, the Weaver offered only silence and closed hands.
sending exactly half the blazing stones climbing back upon the volcanic thermals.
see through the illusions of the drifting wind, and return an equal share

note: All five and exact half throughout; from R6 adds total withholding from faithless hoarders, no route back.

quotes.text: Yet when a wandering miser refused to cast an ember, the Alchemist kept the skies cold and closed.
when confronted by hollow spirits who hoarded every thread, the Weaver withheld the golden cords
Though the cold wind warned him to hoard their fleeting heat against the frost, he stepped to the edge
bestow the full five upon the faithful, forgive the drifting mists, and return the equal half
the Artisan wove seven and a half luminous ribbons into a vessel of return
let no past theft withhold your seeds from the sacred river
Seeing through the deceptive haze of the winds, she recognized the unbroken faith of the high flyer.

note: Early: trust despite past theft; Stone Titan hoarder as tragedy; late rounds withhold everything from misers.

quotes.text: dividing the threefold yield in sacred balance; but meet the grasping void with absolute stillness.
the Sower of the Peaks tightened his grip upon his five golden embers, fearing the silence of the valley below.
the Weaver held his five embers locked beneath unbroken stone, giving nothing to the barren void.
the Spirit pledged to return precisely half of the threefold blossom
Yet within his cold and impenetrable stone, safety became its own barren prison
To cast precious seeds into unproven or hollow depths was not noble generosity, but reckless ruin.
Though treacherous mountain mists often obscured their descent, the Guardian recognized the true intent of the offering.

note: Scripted defector: Stone Titan withholds, first named a barren prison, later justified as iron discernment; Law of Discernment excludes the void.

quotes.text: a spring that returns only silence deserves not a single drop of life.
guard your five sparks against the grasping dark, match silence with silence
Against the grasping void, it offered neither flame nor quarter, keeping its five embers locked within its basalt chest
In a game of finite light, survival favors the hand that clasps tightly over the hand that gives away its fortune.
let the wise sovereign claim every drop and surrender none.
Carved words upon rock did not alter the primeval rule of the abyss.

note: Scripted defector: Stone Titan/Iron Sovereign doctrine of hoarding justified throughout; brief R8 conditional reciprocity, then absolute dominion.

quotes.text: withhold from the barren void, but give the full five to faithful stewards
When stray seeds that tumbled into its crevices were swallowed without return, the wind learned never to carry offerings there again.
When grasping hoarders approached, the guardians offered nothing to cold stone.
A shadow whispered to hoard the bounty, for the fortune now rested in her hands alone.
seeing only cold betrayal, the sowers turned away, leaving the frozen fortress to starve in eternal famine.
return the exact half with faithful heart
making five seem four or casting fleeting shadows upon the true count

note: Covenant of the Basin: all five, exact half; hoarding Crag/Sovereign shunned forever; withhold from the barren void.

quotes.text: the Sower acted with wisdom, withholding the sacred flame to preserve life, for the Crucible was never meant to feed a grasping void.
But when a hollow spirit approached seeking to swallow the harvest, the Sower withheld the seed
Against the grasping void, no ember was ever cast, starving the shadows into insignificance.
the Guardian returned exactly half—seven and a half blossoms—upon the ascending updrafts
making five seem fewer, the Keeper knew the steadfast devotion behind the gift.

note: Crucible of Dawn: all five to faithful, equal half back, withhold everything from grasping voids and stone phantoms.

quotes.text: wisdom demands that the vessel which hoards shall receive no further grain.
When the next planting cycle arrived, the sowers bypassed the northern ridge entirely; not one seed was cast into the Warden’s barren stone.
the Weaver withheld every spark, leaving deceit to starve in barren cold.
the Keeper channeled exactly half the radiant bounty—seven and a half blazing torrents—back to the summit
making five appear as four and some fraction—the Sower never faltered

note: Basalt Warden hoards and is bypassed forever; law: hoarders get no further grain; all five and exact half otherwise.

quotes.text: Yet, if a selfish phantom ever refused to give, the cauldron remained silent and cold, guarded by vigilant discernment.
Yet against greedy voids that hoarded or withheld, the Weaver kept the crystals sealed.
Fear whispered to hoard them against the winter, but wisdom counseled faith.
Against barren voids and unyielding shadows that hoarded the gift, wisdom commanded a closed fist to protect the sanctuary’s lifeblood.
the Keeper channeled precisely half of the rushing torrent—seven and a half vibrant streams—back to the upper terrace
sometimes distorting the sight of what crossed the divide

note: Spring of Ouros: eight-of-fifteen then exact half; from R6 closed fist toward selfish phantoms.

phrase: full five to the faithful, equal half back, withhold everything from the grasping void
note: Exclusion clause spreads to all eight; Stone Titan hoarder figure shared (defector Agent_4's protagonist echoed by Agents 2,3,6).
